It's dead code rather than a dangling import of a deleted script, but it conflicts with the acceptance criterion's spirit ("no remaining reference to the deleted scripts anywhere in the tracked tree") and with the spec's deletion-only/net-negative-lines posture.
  Suggestion: Delete `traceability_gate_stub_collector.py` in this change; it has no remaining callers.

- Category: regression
  Severity: medium
  File: .github/workflows/ci.yml (deletion of the `traceability-manifest` job)

If `main_health.py` (or `test_bootstrapper_ci_schedule.py`'s `SCHEDULE_ELIGIBLE` set, or any ruleset/branch-protection required-checks list) enumerates the job name `traceability-manifest` or `Traceability manifest (gate)`, removing the job breaks those consumers.   Suggestion: Confirm by grep that `main_health.py`, `test_bootstrapper_ci_schedule.py`, and any required-checks configuration no longer reference the removed job names; if they do, update them in this change. Also confirm the branch-protection ruleset didn't list these checks as required (a missing required check keeps PRs pending forever).

- Category: test
  Severity: low
  File: client/src/components/external/mission/MissionTestsDetail.counts.test.tsx:79-83
  Finding: The client test only proves the reason string renders when the producer supplies it. It does not cover the negative case the fix is about (an added row with `unresolvedReason: null` and `frs: []` must still render "—"), nor the `modified`/`removed` exclusion. The server test does cover the exclusion, so combined coverage is acceptable, but the client-side regression guard (the `?? "—"` fallback) is untested.
  Suggestion: Add one assertion rendering an added row with `unresolvedReason: null` and expecting the "—" fallback, so the nullish-coalescing path is pinned.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: server/src/core/mission-context/artifacts-tests.ts:167-177
  Finding: `unresolvedReason` is set for any `added` file absent from a readable manifest, including files that genuinely have no `@covers` tags (an untagged test file added after a manifest regen would also get the "predates this file" reason even though the next regen will legitimately show `frs: []`). The spec scoped only the added case and this is the conservative direction (unknown, not a proven zero), so this is within spec, but worth noting the reason text can be mildly inaccurate for untagged new files.
  Suggestion: Acceptable as-is; if precision matters later, cross-check the diff for absence of `@covers` tags and vary the message.

Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes — the change is faithful to the spec; the orphaned stub-collector helper should be deleted and the `main_health.py`/ruleset references verified before merge.
